Curiosity shrub: tiny flowers and black berries sit on the leaf midrib; berries need male and female plants.
Evergreen with narrow leaves bearing flowers and black berries on the midrib; for sheltered, moist shade.
Night-opening, fragrant lemon-yellow trumpets; the buds are a Chinese vegetable ('golden needles').
Neat evergreen clumps with sprays of tiny coral-red bells; the best flowering Heuchera; needs drainage.
Large, hairy, maple-like leaves; copes with heat and humidity better than most; airy flowers in late summer.
Heuchera × Tiarella hybrids: colourful evergreen leaves and frothy flowers; more shade-tolerant than Heuchera.
Dinner-plate flowers up to 25 cm in late summer; shoots appear very late (May); never let it dry out.
Narrow, glossy dark green leaves in dense mounds; lilac bells on tall stems; tough edging for shade.
Fast-spreading groundcover for wet soil and pond edges; aromatic leaves used as a herb in Asia; contain it.
Smaller, hardier relative of the mophead, mostly with lacecaps; flowers on old wood, so prune lightly.
Big velvety leaves and wide lacecaps of lilac fertile and pale outer flowers; peeling bark; shelter from wind.
Formerly Schizophragma; self-clinging, with creamy lacecaps a few weeks after climbing hydrangea; slow start.
Evergreen groundcover with large golden saucers all summer; spreads fast; shear to the ground every few years.
Yellow summer flowers followed by glossy berries prized by florists; cut back hard in early spring.
Small yellow flowers, then berries turning red to black; tolerates shade and damp; self-seeds freely.
Low, arching semi-evergreen with large golden flowers and red anthers; cut back hard in spring; needs shelter.
Very hardy dwarf shrub with narrow blue-green leaves and fluffy yellow flowers; takes drought and lime.
Low grey-green sub-shrub with large golden stars; for rock gardens, walls and gravel in full sun.
Very hardy holly with glossy blue-green spiny leaves and purple stems; red berries on females near a male.
Hybrid holly with large, glossy, toothed leaves; vigorous, makes a dense screen or specimen.
Vigorous hybrid holly with large, often nearly spineless leaves; tolerates pollution and coastal wind.
Slow, narrow holly with small, squarish, spiny leaves pressed along the stems; red berries on females.
Low, spreading holly from forest understoreys; very shade-tolerant; red berries on female plants.
Rosy-pink trumpets over fern-like leaves in late spring; mark the spot, it emerges very late; good drainage.
Sold as 'Gerardiana': airy shrub with ferny leaves and rosy-purple pea flowers all summer; leafs out late.
Flat, saucer-sized flowers in June–July; needs lime-free soil, wet in summer but drier in winter.
Grey-green sword leaves and fragrant pale lavender flowers; its rhizomes are the source of orris root.
Violet-blue flowers with white-veined, yellow-based falls; for pond margins and boggy soil.
Evergreen fans spreading by runners; frilled, orchid-like pale lilac flowers in spring; needs winter shelter.
Sold as a white form: flat, open flowers in early summer; loves wet soil and pond edges; feed well.

origin: Garden hybrid (Iberian and N African parents)
notes: Classic florists' iris from bulbs planted in autumn; needs sharp drainage and a warm, sunny spot.
Fragrant white bottlebrush flowers in early summer and brilliant red autumn leaves; likes moist soil.
Bright yellow flowers on bare green stems from late winter; train on a wall or let it cascade over banks.
Sold as 'Angel Wing': glossy evergreen with fragrant white star flowers; grow in a pot, winter frost-free.
Large timber tree with hard-shelled, tasty nuts; strong juglone toxicity harms many plants nearby.
Very hardy American walnut with oily, sweet, elongated nuts; shorter-lived and prone to butternut canker.
Native rush for pond edges and bog gardens; evergreen green stems, also grows in shallow water.
Stiff blue-grey stems for pond margins and wet ground; copes with drier soil once settled.
Variable conifer, conical to bushy; tolerates heat, drought and city air. Alternate host of pear rust.
Tough conical tree for windbreaks; blue berries for birds; foliage bronzes in winter.
Prickly two-banded needles and red-brown berries; for hot, dry, stony sites; dislikes wet winters.
Wide, flat-topped shrub with arching tiers; covers banks fast. Alternate host of pear rust.
Low mat of soft blue-green needles for banks, wall tops and rock gardens.
Prickly, bright blue-green mat from seaside dunes; thrives in sandy, poor soil and salt spray.
Very hardy, low spreading juniper with scale and needle leaves; for sunny banks and rockeries.

origin: E Siberia, N China, Korea, Japan
notes: Small asters from June to September; compact, needs no staking. Divide every few years.
Spreading Japanese aster with pale lilac daisies in late summer; young leaves eaten in Japan.
Wiry stems with small white daisies over a long late-summer season; good filler and cut flower.
Nodding waxy yellow bells in late summer over maple-like leaves; needs acid, moist, shady soil.
Late, rounded orange-red heads fading yellow, Sept–Nov; broad evergreen leaves. Mulch in winter.
Compact blue-grey tufts for sand, gravel and rock gardens; silvery panicles ripen golden.
Native small tree with long hanging golden chains in May; all parts, esp. seeds, are poisonous.
Flowers two weeks after common laburnum, with longer, slimmer chains; glossy leaves. All parts toxic.
Crinkled flower panicles in late summer, mottled bark; needs heat. Leafs out late, often in June.
Native woodland carpet with yellow hooded flowers; spreads fast by runners under trees.
Fast deciduous conifer with blue-green needles, orange-gold autumn colour and reddish twigs.
Fast, shrubby mallow flowering all summer; short-lived. Cut back in spring, shelter from wind.
Fine-needled evergreen smothered in small flowers; not frost-hardy here, grow in pots of acid compost.
Prairie perennial with silky leaves and creamy clover heads; fixes nitrogen, copes with drought.
Arching wands of rosy-purple pea flowers in early autumn; cut to the ground in spring.
Rosy-purple pea flowers from July into autumn; tolerates poor dry soil. Prune hard in spring.
Arching evergreen with leathery leaves, bronze-red in winter; needs acid, moist, humus-rich soil.
Arching evergreen for acid woodland soil; hanging white bells in May, purplish in winter.
Low evergreen with glossy pointed leaves turning red in winter; for acid, moist soil in shade.
Hollow bamboo-like stems; hanging white flowers in claret bracts, then purple berries for birds.
Broad steel-blue leaves for sand and gravel; spreads aggressively, so plant in a sunk barrier.
Dense purple spikes open from the top down; butterfly magnet and long-lasting cut flower.
Evergreen iris-like fans that turn orange in cold weather; small white flowers in late spring.
Slender yellow spires on dark stems over deeply cut leaves; needs moist soil and midday shade.
Big rounded leaves and orange daisies in late summer; wilts in hot sun, needs constantly moist soil.
Huge, deeply lobed leaves and orange-yellow daisies in early summer; for pond sides and damp shade.
Small-leaved, semi-evergreen privet with white flowers and black berries; clips well.
Glossy evergreen privet for hedges and topiary; scented white panicles. Needs a mild site here.
Large evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy leaves and big white panicles; invasive in warm areas.
Tiny grass-like carpeter for aquariums and pond shallows; not frost-hardy, overwinter indoors.
Upward-facing, unscented flowers in early summer; easy and hardy. Watch for red lily beetle.
Aromatic leaves, tiny yellow flowers before the leaves, clear yellow autumn; red berries on females.
Three-lobed leaves turn butter-yellow in autumn; yellow flower clusters on bare twigs in March.
Three-lobed leaves open purplish and turn red to purple in autumn; less hardy than American sweet gum.
Slow, smaller tree with small, deeply lobed leaves, orange to red in autumn; source of storax resin.
Three-lobed leaves flush burgundy in spring and turn red-purple in autumn; slender, fast tree.
Fast tree with deeply waisted leaves, yellow in autumn; smaller green-yellow flowers than L. tulipifera.
Evergreen grassy clumps with violet bead spikes in autumn; edging for shade. Cut old leaves in March.
Narrow grassy evergreen leaves and pale violet spikes in late summer; spreads to a lawn-like cover.
Hardier, faster-spreading lilyturf with narrow leaves and pale lilac spikes; vigorous groundcover.
Evergreen sub-shrubby mat with gentian-blue flowers; needs acid, well-drained soil and shelter.
Upright flower spikes in summer for moist borders and pond edges; often short-lived, mulch in winter.
Low, horizontal evergreen for shade under trees; small violet berries; trims into low hedges.
Twining honeysuckle with pink-and-yellow scented trumpets all summer; aphids in dry spots.
Tubular orange-red flowers, then shiny black berries in red bracts; tough, also for coasts.
Tough, very hardy flowering shrub with red berries for birds; can self-seed, invasive in N America.
Very fragrant cream flowers on bare twigs from December to March; plant by a path or door.
Large tiered shrub with scented white-to-yellow flowers and red autumn berries; invasive in N America.
Vigorous semi-evergreen twiner; very scented white flowers ageing yellow. Invasive in warm regions.
Twining climber with unscented scarlet trumpets over a long season; blue-green leaves.
Deciduous hemiparasite of oaks and sweet chestnut with yellow berries; grows only on a host branch.
Evergreen with spidery fringe flowers in spring, white in the wild form; acid soil, shelter or pots.
Native dry-meadow perennial with sticky stems and magenta flower heads in May–June.
Tiny rock-garden plant: tufts of narrow leaves and pink-magenta flower heads; needs grit.
Arching, thorny shrub with purple flowers and red berries Aug–Oct; suckers freely.
Goji relative with softer, broader leaves; edible red berries and young shoots. Suckers.
Nodding yellow stars over fringed leaves; spreads by rhizomes in moist soil.
Arching white spikes like a flock of geese; bronze autumn leaves. Spreads fast, needs a barrier.
Native marsh plant with fluffy yellow flower tufts in the leaf axils; for bogs and 0–5 cm water.
Towering grey-green lobed leaves and buff plumes in summer; spreads by runners, give it room.
Thorny, drought-proof tree with glossy leaves; female trees bear big green, inedible 'oranges'.
Starry, lightly scented flowers on bare branches in April; lime-tolerant, flowers young.
Pure white, fragrant goblets on bare branches in early spring; prone to late-frost damage.
Nodding, scented white cups with crimson stamens from June; acid soil and light shade.
Very hardy, large magnolia; greenish-yellow flowers among the leaves, cucumber-like red fruit.
Huge leaves (to 50 cm) clustered like umbrellas; creamy, oddly scented flowers, red fruit cones.
Shrubby magnolia with slender purple goblets as the leaves unfold; late enough to miss most frosts.
Rare hybrid; spiny, glossy evergreen leaves of two shapes, bronze in winter; yellow spring flowers.
Bold, spiny pinnate leaves; upright spikes of scented yellow flowers in winter feed early bees.
Soft, spineless narrow leaflets and yellow flower spikes in autumn; neat in shade or pots.
Spreading sprays of lily-of-the-valley-scented pale yellow flowers in winter; for shade.
Stiff blue-green spiny leaflets; upright yellow racemes in early spring, then blue-black berries.
Soft, woolly round leaves with a fruity apple-mint scent; spreads, so grow it in a sunk pot.
Native silver-grey mint with lilac spikes, a bee magnet; strong scent. Spreads in damp soil.
Low native mint with flowers in leaf whorls; high-menthol forms are used in Asian cooking.
Twining climber with glossy pinnate leaves and sprays of small creamy flowers in July–August.
Lavender snapdragon-like flowers June–August on square stems; for pond margins and bog gardens.
Sterile giant to 3 m or more; quick summer screen that rustles in the wind; flowers only in hot years.
Tall, broad-leaved silver grass for screening; often confused with M. × giganteus; flowers after hot summers.
Native of damp heaths; purplish flower sprays, butter-yellow autumn; stems break off in winter.
Wiry stems with tiny round leaves form a dense mat that spills over walls; shelter from hard frost.
Fine, tidy clump with airy rosy-pink flower clouds in autumn; needs sharp drainage in winter.
Maple-like leaves, bronze in spring and red in autumn; white flower sprays in April; for moist shade.
Hardiest banana: frost kills the stem but roots regrow; wrap or mulch over winter; shelter from wind.
Hardy Himalayan banana; leaves often flushed red beneath; mulch the base heavily over winter.
Squat banana with a long-lasting golden lotus-like flower; mulch heavily or overwinter frost-free.
Bamboo-like evergreen; white flower sprays, then red berries into winter; leaves redden in cold.
Arching canes with drooping spikes of small pink flowers in late spring; thin old stems after flowering.
Taller, greener catmint with larger blue flowers; cut back after the first flush to repeat.
Among the first shrubs to leaf and flower: drooping white tassels in early spring; separate sexes.
Huge lemon-yellow cups open in the evening above sprawling stems; needs sharp drainage, hates wet winters.
Slow evergreen tufts of strap leaves; tiny lilac bells, then berries; spreads slowly by runners.
Dense dark green tufts spreading by runners; evergreen lawn substitute for shade; tender in hard winters.
Aromatic glossy leaves turn a striking pale yellow, almost white, in autumn; tough and shade tolerant.
Holly-like spiny evergreen; tiny, very fragrant white flowers in autumn; slow and clips well.
Hornbeam-like tree with hop-like fruit clusters; tough on dry limestone; good street and park tree.
Tree-peony flowers on a herbaceous plant: dies back in winter; strong stems need no staking; long season.
Rare Chinese relative of Persian ironwood; fiery autumn colour and mottled, flaking bark.
Velvety leaves with silvery veins, best in shade; crimson autumn; self-clinging and less rampant.
Fast tree; large creamy, purple-spotted foxglove flowers before the leaves; less hardy than P. tomentosa.
Smaller paulownia with violet-blue, yellow-throated flowers; sticky leaves; needs a warm, sheltered site.
Long season of soft, pinkish bottlebrush plumes from June; needs sun and drainage. Syn. Cenchrus orientalis.
Damp-meadow native; dense pink pokers in early summer over broad leaves; spreads. Syn. Persicaria bistorta.
Foliage plant for part shade; wiry sprays of tiny red flowers in late summer; can self-seed freely.
Mat-forming; short pink pokers from midsummer; leaves turn russet and persist through winter.
Creeping and tender; round pink flower heads, chevron-marked leaves; often grown as an annual; self-seeds.
Native of riverbanks; invasive runners, so plant in a sunken container; thrives in wet soil.
Chinese species with racemes of single white flowers in June; little scent; vigorous, arching shrub.
Evergreen needle-leaved mats smothered in flowers in spring; for rockeries, walls and slopes.
Tighter, smaller and earlier than moss phlox; tiny cushions for troughs, crevices and rockeries.
Cylindrical flower heads on purple-spotted stems; earlier and more mildew resistant than garden phlox.
Bold evergreen fans of sword leaves; hardy to about −10 °C, so overwinter in pots or cover well.
Hardy running bamboo with yellow-grooved green canes; install a root barrier 60–70 cm deep.
One of the hardiest, densest bamboos; dark green leaves; ideal screen or hedge; needs a root barrier.
Spikes of hinged pink snapdragon-like flowers in late summer; spreads by runners in moist soil.
Very hardy spruce with blue-green, pungent needles; dislikes hot, dry summers; parent of 'Conica'.
Elegant spruce with very short, glossy dark needles; copes with drought better than Norway spruce.
Curtains of hanging branchlets; slow when young; needs cool, moist air and soil, not hot dry sites.
Fast forestry spruce with sharp blue-green needles; needs cool, humid air; too big for most gardens.
Picturesque, often leaning pine with orange-red bark and soft bright green needles.
Hardy five-needle pine with flexible shoots and blue-green needles; tolerates wind and drought.
Fast five-needle pine with soft blue-green needles; dislikes lime and dry wind; prone to blister rust.
Tree-form relative of dwarf mountain pine with hooked cone scales; very hardy, wind and lime tolerant.
Low, wide shrubby form of mountain pine, 2–3 m after many years; greyish-white young candles.
Dense, narrow five-needle pine from Balkan mountains; very hardy and healthy; slow-growing.
Five-needle pine with twisted blue-green needles and tiered branches; classic Japanese-garden tree.
Long, soft grey-green needles droop gracefully; long resinous cones; needs space and shelter.
Long, stiff blue-green needles and large cones; bark smells of vanilla when warm; drought tolerant.
Dense, dark Balkan pine with grey, plated bark; very tolerant of lime, drought and heat. Syn. P. leucodermis.
Wavy-edged leaves on black stems; tiny dark, honey-scented flowers in spring; tender below about −10 °C.
Long-lived village-square tree of the Balkans; deeply cut leaves; flaking bark; needs lots of room.
Huge tree with white patches on the upper bark; prone to anthracnose in Europe, where London plane is tougher.
Umbrella-like leaves hide nodding white flowers; spreads into colonies in woodland shade; toxic.
Lavender-blue cups over ladder-like leaves; self-seeds; cut back after flowering for a second flush.
Low woodland Jacob's ladder; nodding sky-blue bells in spring; likes humus-rich soil that stays moist.
Very glossy, dark evergreen fronds; new fronds unroll backwards like tassels; for moist shade.
Compact evergreen fern with dark, lacy fronds; for rock crevices, shady edging and pots.
Large, leathery evergreen fronds in bold clumps; copes with dry shade once established.
Stiff, harsh-textured evergreen fronds in a neat shuttlecock; for shady borders and woodland.
Syn. Poncirus trifoliata. Hardy, very thorny citrus: green stems, scented flowers, bitter yellow fruit.
Very fast, large poplar with triangular leaves; female trees shed cotton; roots invade drains.
Fast hybrid black poplar for windbreaks and timber; plant well away from buildings and drains.
Rare Chinese poplar for collections; fast-growing, needs the space of a park or large garden.
Rare collector's poplar with large leaves, pale bluish beneath; give it moist soil and room.

origin: S & C Europe, N Africa, C Asia
notes: Leaves white-felted beneath, flickering silver in wind; suckers widely – not for small gardens.
Native floodplain poplar with a broad, heavy crown; fast; for riversides and shelterbelts.
Very hardy Siberian balsam poplar with narrow leaves and sticky, resin-scented buds.
Hardy, fast, narrow-crowned hybrid balsam poplar for windbreaks and avenues in cold regions.
Leaves tremble in the faintest breeze; clear yellow autumn colour; suckers freely.
Natural white poplar × aspen hybrid; grey-felted leaves; tolerates wet, heavy soil; suckers.
Velvety, strawberry-like leaves under large buttercup-yellow flowers; for edges and rock gardens.
Loose sprays of saucer flowers all summer over strawberry-like leaves; sun and good drainage.
Silky, silvery strawberry-like leaves and blood-red flowers on lax stems; for sunny borders.
Ball-shaped flower heads on stout stems in early spring; needs soil that never dries out.
Candelabra primula with tiers of orange flowers from red buds; for bog gardens and pond margins.
Candelabra primula with whorls of magenta, yellow-eyed flowers; for wet, part-shaded spots.
Robust candelabra primula for bog gardens; whorls of flowers in late spring; self-seeds.
Poker-like spikes, red in bud, opening lilac; short-lived – needs cool, moist, humus-rich soil.
Syn. Pritzelago alpina: low glossy cushions smothered in pure white flowers; for troughs and scree.
Tiny, strongly mint-scented evergreen leaves; white bells flecked purple; protect in hard winters.
Small shrub wreathed in flowers in spring; cut flowered shoots hard back right after bloom.
Pink rosettes cover bare twigs in April; prune flowered shoots hard right after bloom (monilia).
Fragrant blossom on bare twigs in late winter; plant in a warm, sheltered spot against frost.
Ground-hugging cherry for slopes and banks; white spring flowers, small black fruit, red autumn leaves.
Small, twiggy cherry with nodding white-pink flowers in March; fine autumn colour; bonsai favourite.
Sweet × sour cherry hybrids; white blossom, then mild, juicy cherries for eating and cooking.
Rare Chinese wild cherry for collections; pale spring blossom on a small tree.
Single pink blossom with bronze young leaves; among the earliest and finest red autumn colours.
Very hardy small tree; white flower spikes, then dark astringent berries loved by birds; suckers.
Compact shrub with deep red-purple leaves all season; pale pink flowers; clips into colour hedges.
Early-flowering plum with large, juicy fruit; most cultivars need another Japanese plum to pollinate.
Self-fertile; fruits on last year's shoots – prune every spring; spray against peach leaf curl.
Tough, often self-fertile cherry for jam, juice and strudel; tolerates poor soil; may sucker.
Glossy leaves, white racemes, black cherries for birds; invasive in Central European woods – take care.
Small, tough plum for jam and spirits; suckers; also used as a hardy rootstock and hedgerow tree.
Flaking camouflage bark, pink spring flowers and huge fragrant yellow fruit for jelly; red autumn leaves.
Slow deciduous conifer; soft needles turn golden-orange in autumn; wants acid to neutral soil.
Fast, very tall forest conifer with soft, fruity-scented needles; only for parks and large gardens.
Small tree with aromatic trifoliate leaves, sweet-scented flowers and round winged seeds; yellow in autumn.
Rare small tree, often multi-stemmed, with drooping panicles of fragrant white flowers; lime-free soil.
Fine needle leaves and flat heads of white flowers that swarm with insects; minty when brushed.
Downy, strongly mint-scented leaves; flat heads of pale lilac flowers, a top bee plant; spreads slowly.
Silver-dusted bracts around small pinkish flowers draw countless pollinators; spreads by rhizomes.
Asian pear with crisp, juicy fruit eaten firm; needs another pear nearby for pollination.
Pyramidal oak with deeply cut leaves turning scarlet; lower branches droop; dislikes chalky soil.
Slow, shrubby small oak with large, chestnut-like toothed leaves; yellow-brown autumn colour.
Oak with entire, glossy laurel-like leaves; russet autumn colour; dry leaves often hang on in winter.
Glossy, chestnut-like leaves with bristle-tipped teeth; fast for an oak; golden-brown in autumn.
Syn. Q. prinus. Wavy-toothed, chestnut-like leaves and deeply ridged bark; copes with dry, rocky soil.
White oak × English oak hybrids: vigorous and mildew-resistant, often reddish in autumn.
Upright hybrid oaks with glossy, mildew-resistant leaves; narrow trees for streets and smaller gardens.
Rose-like layered flowers from claw-shaped tubers; plant in spring, lift before frost.
Flat silver mat of tiny rosettes for scree, troughs and paving; needs sharp drainage, no winter wet.
Tight silver-grey moss-like carpet for troughs and crevices; gritty soil, shelter from winter wet.
Silver, finely cut leaves and daisies from spring to autumn; needs sharp drainage and winter dryness.
Tough shrub for shade; white four-petalled flowers, then shiny black beads that last into winter.
Low suckering shrub with aromatic three-part leaves, yellow catkins in spring and fiery autumn colour.
Velvety antler-like shoots, red fruit cones and blazing autumn colour; suckers aggressively.
Source of the tangy red sumac spice; downy pinnate leaves turn red in autumn; for hot, dry slopes.
Very hardy currant with drooping yellowish flower tassels, black berries and crimson autumn colour.
Hanging pink-red flower clusters in April, early bee food; blue-black berries; prune after flowering.
Bristly shrub with large rose-pink pea flowers; often grafted on a stem; brittle – shelter from wind.
Bronze-flushed, chestnut-like leaves and plumes of pink flowers; needs moist soil and wind shelter.
Big jagged leaflets, bronze in spring and red-brown in autumn; creamy flower plumes; for wet shade.
Large, shapely blooms mostly one per long stem; prune hard in spring and feed for repeat flushes.
Clusters of medium blooms almost non-stop June to frost; plant in groups of 3–5 or as a low hedge.
Low bushes with big trusses of small blooms all summer; tough, compact roses for edging and bedding.
Bushy, robust roses for borders and informal hedges; only light pruning; most repeat-flower.
Stiff, mostly repeat-flowering canes for walls, pillars and arches; tie in near-horizontal for more flowers.

origin: Garden origin (mostly R. multiflora & R. wichurana hybrids)
notes: Long, pliable canes for trees, pergolas and fences; huge sprays of small flowers, mostly once in summer.

Tall, tough old roses with grey-green leaves and scented white to blush flowers once in June.

Arching wild rose with scented single white flowers in June–July, then red hips; very hardy, drought-tolerant.
Tender aquatic for pond margins, tubs and aquaria; creeping stems root at the nodes; overwinter indoors.
Suckering subshrub with white flowers and large, mild red fruit held above the leaves; contain the runners.
Arching canes that root at the tips instead of suckering; rich-flavoured black berries in early summer.
Grown for white-bloomed winter stems and ferny grey leaves; cut all canes to the ground every spring.
Hairier, more drought-tolerant than 'Goldsturm'; golden daisies with dark cones July to October.
Tall prairie daisy with yellow rays and brown cones in late summer; leaves smell of anise when crushed.

origin: C & E Europe to Siberia and Korea
notes: Low native willow of wet meadows and sands with narrow silvery leaves; spring catkins feed early bees.

origin: Europe, N Africa, W & C Asia
notes: Native osier with slender purple stems and blue-green leaves; for basketry, hedges and wet ground.
Large shrubby willow with silvery spring catkins; best known for its fasciated forms used by florists.

Chinese willow with glossy red-brown shoots, large leaves and showy catkins; good winter stems.

Low bog willow with narrow leaves felted white beneath; extremely hardy; reddish catkins in spring.

origin: NE Turkey, Caucasus; as S. × fragilis across Europe
notes: Crack willow: brittle twigs snap off at the base; glossy leaves; fast tree for riverbanks and wet ground.

Broad shrub with large silky grey catkins turning pink and gold in early spring; cut stems for vases.
Low spreading willow with silky silver leaves; a dune native for sandy banks and coastal sites.
Shrubby sages between S. greggii and S. microphylla; flowers June to frost; needs sharp drainage.
Native mountain elder: creamy flower cones in April, bright red berries in summer (toxic raw).
Tall, airy burnet with slender, nodding bottlebrush spikes in late summer; moist soil.
Grey-green pinnate leaves and arching, fluffy pink spikes in summer; moist soil in sun.
Bold, toothed blue-green leaves and long, drooping, fluffy pink spikes in summer; moist soil.
Trailing mats smothered in small pink flowers in May–June; walls and rockeries; trim after flowering.
Old cottage-garden plant with clove-scented pale pink flowers; spreads by runners; roots lather.

Glossy evergreen for shade; tiny cream flowers fill the air with vanilla scent in winter; black berries.
Narrow, willow-like evergreen leaves; greenish-white, lightly scented winter flowers; least hardy sweet box.
Suckering evergreen with narrow leaves and honey-scented white winter flowers; dense cover in shade.

origin: NE China, Korea, Russian Far East, Japan
notes: Twining climber with scented cream flowers in May, then red 'five-flavour' berries; most need a partner.
Self-clinging climber for shady walls and trees; flat white lacecaps with single large bracts in July.
Gladiolus-like spikes of scarlet stars in autumn (syn. Schizostylis); moist soil and a winter mulch.
Very slow conifer with whorls of glossy needles like umbrella spokes; needs acid, moist soil.
Tall rush for shallow pond margins (syn. Scirpus lacustris); round green stems, brown spikelets; spreads.
Native mat of tiny cylindrical leaves in six rows; green roofs, wall tops, gravel and rock gardens.
Fleshy grey-green clumps under flat pink heads in late summer; butterfly plant; seed heads last.
